featured.name: CORe Pico 4
featured.description: The newest model from CORe Technologies, the makers of Ember. Small and quick, holds a conversation well and can use the helper's tools.

featured.name: CORe Pico V3
featured.description: The previous Pico from CORe Technologies. Steady in long conversations and can think step by step when you ask it to.

featured.name: LFM2.5 1.2B
featured.description: Liquid AI's small all-rounder. Very fast even without a graphics card, and a good first model for older computers.

featured.name: LFM2.5 VL 1.6B
featured.description: Looks at pictures and screenshots. Pick this when you want Ash to read what is on the screen or describe an image.

featured.name: LFM2.5 2.6B
featured.description: A noticeable step up in quality while still running comfortably on an ordinary laptop.

featured.name: Qwen3.5 4B
featured.description: Alibaba's well-known small model. Strong at reasoning and tool use, and it can also look at pictures.

advanced.name: LFM2.5 350M
advanced.description: Tiny and instant. Fine for quick questions on very weak hardware, but expect simple answers.

advanced.name: LFM2.5 1.2B Thinking
advanced.description: The small Liquid AI model trained to think before it answers. Slower, but better at puzzles and maths.

advanced.name: Qwen3.5 0.8B
advanced.description: The smallest Qwen3.5. Can look at pictures even on low-memory machines.

advanced.name: Qwen3.5 2B
advanced.description: A middle ground between speed and quality, with picture support.

advanced.name: LFM2.5 8B-A1B
advanced.description: A larger mixture-of-experts model that only wakes a small part of itself per word, so it stays fast. Wants around 6 GB of free memory.

advanced.name: Qwen3.5 9B
advanced.description: The best quality here and the heaviest. Needs roughly 8 GB of free memory, ideally on a graphics card.
